# Migraine Surgical Interventions

**Authors:** Jitin Bajaj, Joe M. Das, Sunil Munakomi

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Migraine is a primary neurologic disorder characterized by recurrent headache, often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia, or vertigo, and may present with or without aura. The condition affects 11.7% of the United States population, including 17.1% of women and 5.6% of men. Migraine can be episodic, acute, or chronic. Pharmacologic treatment includes β-blockers, anticonvulsants, calcium channel blockers, tricyclic antidepressants, and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Migraine surgery is indicated when the condition is refractory to medical treatment. Chronic migraine is defined by the International Headache Society classification of headache disorders, third edition: Headache occurring ≥15 days/month. Duration > 3 months. Other features of migraine occurring ≥8 days/month.
